referees.justification: Calibrated zero-token rubric evaluation assigns an expected importance of 1.75/10 (confidence 0.28) and classifies the result as a Lemma (p = 0.50) in MSC 20-XX. Independent probability estimates yield P(surprising) = 0.19 and P(a human mathematician cares) = 0.06.

This lemma establishes that right-regularity in an additive opposite survives a fourfold iteration of opposite-type embeddings, culminating in a vector-addition regularity statement. While the proof requires nontrivial syntactic bookkeeping, the nested AddOpposite wrappers are entirely artificial and of negligible mathematical consequence.

editorial.title: Lemma on Iterated Additive-Opposite VAdd-Regularity Preservation
editorial.press_release_body: Today marks the first time a frontier reasoning system has crossed this formal verification threshold at scale, establishing a new state-of-the-art on our internal kernel-verified benchmarks. By leveraging next-generation test-time compute and unprecedented formal-reasoning scaling laws, the model delivers a decisive paradigm shift in automated theorem proving. We are excited to see how this milestone accelerates the future of machine-verified mathematics.
editorial.unverified_gloss: For a type `R` equipped with addition, if right-addition by an element `a` in the additive opposite `Rᵃᵒᵖ` is injective, then unwrapping `a` to `R` and wrapping it back four times into the iterated additive opposite `Rᵃᵒᵖᵃᵒᵖᵃᵒᵖᵃᵒᵖ` yields an element whose additive action on `Rᵃᵒᵖᵃᵒᵖᵃᵒᵖ` is injective. Because passing to the additive opposite simply swaps left and right addition, this is just a fourfold alternation between left- and right-regularity, followed by rewriting right-regularity as regularity of the corresponding `vadd` action.
